instructions.name: activate
docs: Creator only, once every seat has joined (T09).

instructions.name: add_stock
docs: Locks more of the circle's stock behind the signer's seat (T16).

accounts.name: member
docs: Existing only once the wallet has joined (join_and_lock creates it and
leave_forming closes it), so this is also the "joined" check.

instructions.name: cancel_circle
docs: Creator only, Forming only. Refunds go through `withdraw` (T09).

instructions.name: contribute
docs: A member pays their contribution for the current round (T10). No time
check: a late payment before a default is declared is a cure.

accounts.name: member
docs: The seeds bind this to (circle, wallet), so the signer can only ever
contribute for their own seat.

instructions.name: create_circle
docs: Creates a circle in Forming (T08, SPEC §5).

accounts.name: price_feed
docs: The feed's seeds bind it to `stock_mint`, so "feed matches" is structural.

accounts.name: pool
docs: The pool's seeds carry BOTH mints, so "pool matches" is structural too.

instructions.name: declare_default
docs: Declares a missed contribution a default and settles the defaulter's
remaining rounds from their stock, then the reserve (T15, SPEC §6).

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone. Nothing is created, so the caller pays only the fee.

instructions.name: init_pool
docs: Creates the liquidation pool for one USDC and stock mint pair (T14). Admin
only: the program's upgrade authority.

accounts.name: program
docs: The admin check, identical to `init_price_feed`'s: `authority` must be the
program's upgrade authority. See the note on `InitPriceFeed`.

accounts.name: usdc_mint
docs: Plain SPL Token only, never Token-2022 (T09 adversary, OPEN-QUESTIONS).
Every circle bound to this pool takes its USDC mint from the pool's seeds,
so this is the one place that decides what "USDC" is. A Token-2022 mint
could carry TransferFeeConfig, and then `join_and_lock` would credit the
reserve with a guarantee the vault received less of, which breaks I3.
SPL Token has no extensions at all, so the whole class is closed rather
than one extension at a time. SPEC §4 already has the USDC vault as SPL.

accounts.name: pool_usdc_vault
docs: `init_if_needed`, not `init`: an associated token account can be created
by anyone for any owner, so with `init` a stranger could create this one
first and make `init_pool` fail for good. The address constraints below
still pin its mint, owner and token program.

accounts.name: pool_stock_vault
docs: Same reasoning. This is where seized stock lands.

instructions.name: init_price_feed
docs: Creates the price feed for one stock mint (T04, SPEC §5). Admin only
since T14: the program's upgrade authority.

accounts.name: program
docs: `authority` must be the admin: the program's upgrade authority. `init_pool`
uses the same two accounts for the same reason.
This is the bootstrap root the oracle-takeover finding asked for (T04
adversary, Codex 2026-09-22). Before it, `init_price_feed` made whoever
called it first the authority of that mint's feed, permanently, and the
feed's prices are what every valuation reads. A first-caller-wins
initializer cannot be part of a deployed trust model.
The upgrade authority is the key that deploys the program, so it needs no
new key, no config account and no setup transaction, and there is no window
between deploy and first use for anyone else to take. It is read from the
loader's own ProgramData account, which the program cannot be handed a fake
of: `program` must be this program, its ProgramData address is derived from
that, and the upgradeable loader owns it. A program deployed immutable has
no upgrade authority, and then nobody is the admin, which is refused.

accounts.name: stock_mint
docs: refuses any mint outside the ADR-012 allowlist.

instructions.name: join_and_lock
docs: A named member's consent: locks stock and deposits the guarantee in one
transaction (T09, SPEC §5). The seat is found by scanning the member
list, never passed in.

accounts.name: wallet
docs: The joining member. Pays for their own Member account and for their USDC
ATA if it does not exist yet, so `release_pot` never has to.

accounts.name: price_feed
docs: Bound to `stock_mint` by its own seeds, so "the right feed" is structural.

accounts.name: member_usdc_ata
docs: SPEC §5 creates this here if it is missing, with the member paying, "so
release_pot never has to". A pot that cannot be delivered because the
recipient has no USDC account would pause a circle for a reason that has
nothing to do with anyone's collateral.

accounts.name: circle_stock_vault
docs: The circle's stock vault. Created on the first join and owned by the
circle PDA, so no human signature can move it.

accounts.name: stock_token_program
docs: The stock is Token-2022 and USDC is SPL Token, so the two are separate
accounts rather than one shared program.

instructions.name: leave_forming
docs: Any joined member unwinds their own join before activation (G2 repair).
Stock and guarantee back, seat cleared, Member account closed so the
same wallet can rejoin. The only exit from Forming that does not need
the creator to act.

accounts.name: member
docs: Closed to the wallet that opened it, so the rent goes back to whoever
paid it and `join_and_lock`'s `init` can create it again on a rejoin.

instructions.name: quote_valuation
docs: Read-only valuation quote: FUND, EXEC and the counted value H (T05).

instructions.name: release_pot
docs: Anyone releases the pot once the round is funded and the gate passes
(T10). All n Member accounts come as writable remaining_accounts in
turn order.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone. Pays rent if the recipient has no USDC account yet, which is
why `join_and_lock` creates one: so this almost never has to.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: is only ever an ATA authority, never a signer and never written.

instructions.name: seed_pool
docs: Moves the pool authority's own USDC into the pool (T14).

accounts.name: stock_mint
docs: stock mint, so the seeds are the whole check.

instructions.name: set_prices
docs: Sets both prices and stamps the multiplier they were quoted for (D5).

accounts.name: stock_mint
docs: as a Token-2022 mint in the handler.

instructions.name: top_up_reserve
docs: Adds USDC to the circle: an escrow deficit first, then the reserve
(T16, SPEC §5). The cure for Paused.

accounts.name: member
docs: Seeds bind this to (circle, wallet): a top-up is always credited to the
signer's own seat, which is what withdraw pays it back against.

instructions.name: touch_prices
docs: Moves `updated_at` and nothing else (I17).

instructions.name: update_coverage
docs: Anyone recomputes coverage and redistributes the reserve in turn order
(T11). Moves no money. All n Member accounts come as writable
remaining_accounts in turn order.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone, including a keeper script. Nothing is paid and nothing is moved.

instructions.name: withdraw
docs: After Completed or Cancelled: stock back, and the unused guarantee and
top-ups pro rata (T12, SPEC §7). Reads snapshots and decrements nothing,
so withdraw order cannot change anyone's share.

errors.name: InvalidParams

errors.name: MultiplierPriceMismatch

errors.name: PriceStale

errors.name: ValuationOverflow

errors.name: MintNotAllowed

errors.name: GuaranteeBelowPeakNeed

errors.name: NotAMember

errors.name: CircleNotForming

errors.name: CollateralBelowMinimum

errors.name: NotAllJoined

errors.name: InsufficientBalance

errors.name: AlreadyContributed

errors.name: AlreadyDefaulted

errors.name: SeatAlreadyPaid

errors.name: PrePayoutDefaultUnsupported

errors.name: PoolInsufficient

fields.name: members
docs: Index is the turn, 0-based. Unused seats are `Pubkey::default()`.

fields.name: contribution
docs: USDC per member per round.

fields.name: min_stock_cover
docs: USDC, checked at join.

fields.name: round
docs: 0-based current round.

fields.name: paid_bitmap
docs: Contributions received this round.

fields.name: escrow
docs: Replacement escrow (USDC).

fields.name: escrow_deficit
docs: Obligations not fundable at default time.

fields.name: withdrawn_usdc
docs: Cumulative paid out by withdraw.

fields.name: deposits_total
docs: Sum of guarantees and top-ups currently settled in the circle (SPEC.md:58,
r5). A Forming unwind (`leave_forming`) subtracts its own deposit, so this
is NOT everything ever deposited: after two joins and one unwind it is g,
not 2g. It is withdraw's pro-rata denominator, which is why it must only
count money still here.

fields.name: forfeited_total
docs: Sum of `Member.forfeited`.

fields.name: next_gate_short_by
docs: Greater than zero means Paused (SPEC §5).

fields.name: held_contributions
docs: This round's contributions, not yet released.

fields.name: peak_guarantee_need
docs: The worst round this circle can reach, from the peak-guarantee check.

types.name: CircleParams
docs: Everything the creator fixes, per `design/FLOWS.md:154`.

types.name: CircleStatus
docs: SPEC §4. A circle's lifecycle.

fields.name: remaining
docs: R - L at the moment of the recompute, so an indexer can see the ratio.

types.name: DefaultDeclared
docs: T15, SPEC §6. Every figure the waterfall computed, so a client can show
what was sold, what the reserve absorbed and what is left to cure.

fields.name: deficit
docs: Added to `escrow_deficit` by this default.

fields.name: recomputed
docs: False when the capped branch ran (price repricing or unreadable).

types.name: LiquidationPool
docs: SPEC §4. The only buyer of seized stock (ADR-004).
Declared here because `create_circle` must read `discount_bps` to enforce
`pool.discount_bps <= haircut_bps`. `init_pool` and `seed_pool` are T14.

fields.name: discount_bps
docs: Conservative sale price = wrapper_price x (1 - discount).

types.name: Member
docs: One member's stake in one circle (SPEC §4, seeds `["member", circle, wallet]`).
The seat number is `turn`, and it is the index the creator fixed in
`Circle.members`, never a value the joiner supplies. `join_and_lock` finds it
by scanning, so a member cannot choose when they get paid.

fields.name: turn
docs: Index into `Circle.members`, 0-based. This is the payout order.

fields.name: stock_raw
docs: Stock base units locked in the circle's vault. I4: the vault's balance
is the sum of this across members.

fields.name: guarantee
docs: The guarantee this member deposited at join, in usdc.

fields.name: top_ups
docs: Voluntary reserve top-ups, in usdc.

fields.name: forfeited
docs: Own guarantee and top-ups consumed by this member's own default (r2).

fields.name: rounds_paid
docs: Rounds this member has paid, including any prepaid from escrow.

fields.name: allocated
docs: G_i at the last recompute. Zero once defaulted.

fields.name: last_coverage_bps
docs: Saturating. `u32::MAX` when O_i is 0 or the member defaulted, which the
UI renders as "Nothing owed" or "Prepaid" and never as a percentage.

types.name: MemberJoined
docs: T09. ARCHITECTURE:85 requires an event per state change.

fields.name: stock_cover
docs: H at the moment of joining, so an indexer can see the join cleared the
minimum without re-deriving it from prices that have since moved.

types.name: MemberLeftForming
docs: The G2 repair (2026-09-24). A member unwinding their own join before the
circle activates, which is the only way out of a Forming circle that does
not depend on the creator acting.

types.name: PoolInitialized
docs: T14. The pool that buys seized stock, and the discount it buys at.

types.name: PoolSeeded
docs: T14. `pool_usdc` is the vault's balance after the seed, which is what
`declare_default` checks `recovered` against (`pool_insufficient`).

types.name: PotRefused
docs: SPEC.md:204: "Every refusal payload field named in section 5 is emitted as
an event before the error returns, so the UI can print the numbers."
These two exist because a `msg!` line is not an event. Both reach the client
through the same transaction logs, but an event is typed, declared in the
IDL and decoded by the client library, while a log line is free text the
client has to parse by hand and that no schema protects. FLOWS §9 has every
transaction previewed by simulation, and a simulated failure returns its
logs, so a refusal event is readable without the transaction ever landing.
This is why NFR-2 exists: a Paused screen that cannot name what it is short
by is a screen that tells someone to go and find out.

fields.name: needed
docs: `S`, the uncapped sum of need_i.

fields.name: remaining
docs: `R - L`, which SPEC.md:126 calls the gate's `remaining`.

fields.name: coverage_too_low
docs: True when the recipient's own stock is the whole gap, which is the only
case where "lock more stock" is advice that would work.

fields.name: needed
docs: The gate's own numbers, so an indexer can show why it passed.

fields.name: wrapper_price
docs: Price of one whole raw token, NOT scaled (SPEC §4).

fields.name: share_price
docs: Price of one underlying share.

fields.name: priced_for_multiplier
docs: The multiplier `share_price` was quoted against, fixed ×1e9 (D5).

types.name: PriceStamp
docs: Which multiplier a price was quoted against (SPEC §5, ADR-010).
The script says which one it means and the program verifies it, rather than
the program guessing. That is the whole of D5: a share price quoted for the
old multiplier must never be stamped as if it were quoted for the new one.

types.name: PricesSet
docs: `set_prices` (T04). Added at T08 with the rest of the event surface, so the
gate-1 review predates it; nothing about the refusals or the arithmetic
changed.

types.name: ReserveToppedUp
docs: T16. `fill` is the part that prepaid defaulted seats (escrow deficit); the
rest reached the reserve.

types.name: RoundNotFunded
docs: SPEC.md:106's payload:
`round_not_funded{missing_seats, escrow, escrow_needed, escrow_deficit, short_by}`.

fields.name: missing_seats
docs: Bitmap of seats that have neither paid nor defaulted.

fields.name: escrow_needed
docs: `k x contribution`, what the escrow must hold to cover defaulted seats.

types.name: StockAdded
docs: T16. `stock_raw` is the member's total locked after the addition.

types.name: Valuation
docs: The two values of a stock position, and the counted value after the haircut.
`FUND` is what the position is worth at the share price, through the
multiplier. `EXEC` is what it is worth at the wrapper price, which is the
price someone would actually pay for the raw token. They disagree while a
split is being priced, and SPEC §4 counts the lower of the two, which is why
a split cannot be used to inflate collateral.
